item.title: Jonathan Demme’s ‘Married to the Mob’ Arrives on 4K: Why His Pre-‘Silence of the Lambs’ Crime Comedy Is a Must-See
item.description: Cinématographe's 4K debut of the 1988 crime comedy, starring Michelle Pfeiffer and Matthew Modine, offers a new opportunity to examine Demme's transitional film between "Something Wild" and "The Silence of the Lambs."

item.title: Madelaine Petsch Stands by ‘The Strangers’ Spinoff Needing Three Films to Feel Complete
item.description: The actress and producer looked back on her experience releasing the slasher series with IndieWire.

item.title: Tracy Letts Hosts a Very Uncomfortable Family Meal with Elle Fanning and Jamie Bell in First ‘Rosebush Pruning’ Clip — Watch
item.description: Karim Aïnouz's "Fists in the Pocket" reimagining went through a bit of casting musical chairs before landing on an ensemble that also includes Riley Keough, Callum Turner, Pamela Anderson, and Lukas Gage.

item.title: Inside the Casting on Streaming Comedy’s Most Chaotic Improv Show, ‘Very Important People’
item.description: Artios-nominated casting director Jazzy Collins tells IndieWire about the joyful character work behind casting guests for "VIP" and why she'll never stop trying to cast Kristen Wiig.

item.title: ‘Ready or Not 2: Here I Come’ New Trailer: Let Radio Silence Explain the Rules of a New Game
item.description: This time, Samara Weaving faces off with (deep breath) Elijah Wood, Sarah Michelle Gellar, Shawn Hatosy, Nestor Carbonell, and even David Cronenberg.

item.title: Harry Melling Always Wanted to Be a Character Actor — but He’s About to Be a Leading Man
item.description: The former “Harry Potter” star is all about work that is “eccentric and unusual,” and he tells IndieWire why a BDSM relationship comedy with Alexander Skarsgård promised all that, and more.

item.title: The Academy Gets Back Into the Content Business, Led by a Familiar Face
item.description: The Academy has created Academy Studios, which will produce its digital projects and initiatives, and will be led by Jennifer Davidson, now its Chief Marketing, Communications, and Content Officer.

item.description: Neon also acquired William and David Greaves' buzzy doc "Once Upon a Time in Harlem," which could become a major Oscar player.

item.description: "Exorcismo," a new Blu-ray boxed set from Severin, surveys the wildest and most politically committed international genre cinema of the 1970s and early 1980s.

item.description: Wrap your head around the film and TV ecosystem before the creative labor force changes forever.
